previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic back pain, and a history of H. pylori gastritis was admitted with vomiting and worsening back pain after skipping insulin and taking oxycodone without relief. She presented with diabetic ketoacidosis, elevated blood pressure, and tachycardia. Initial management included IV fluids, insulin infusion, and pain control. Labs showed resolving anion gap acidosis and transient leukocytosis, likely due to DKA. Imaging revealed no acute intracranial or abdominal pathology. An endoscopy confirmed H. pylori and chronic gastritis. Her symptoms improved with insulin repletion, antiemetics, and pain management. She tolerated a regular diet without vomiting for over 24 hours and was discharged home on her prior insulin regimen with increased metoclopramide and omeprazole, advised to follow up with gastroenterology and her PCP.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with IDDM who presents with persistent N/V and acute on 
chronic lower back pain.  
  
# N/V: Pt with history of multiple admissions for 
nausea/vomiting secondary to DKA as well as gastroparesis.  She 
presented again with nausea and vomiting associated with back 
pain similar to previous episodes of gastroparesis.  Blood 
glucose ranged widely from ___ at the lowest to 400s depending 
on her po intake.  She was treated with reglan and zofran for 
her emesis and kept NPO with IV hydration.  She was also given a 
short course of erythromycin which was discontinued due to lack 
of effect.  QTc was wnl on erythromycin.  She was able to 
tolerate clears and a BRAT diet intermittently.  She had 
episodes when N/V flared, associated with anxiety, emotional 
distress.  She also reported increase in back pain during these 
episodes.  There appeared to be a large psychosocial component 
as she was completely asymptomatic at times and symptomatic at 
others, often when nearing discharge. Recent workup for similar 
symptoms included CT scans, KUB, UGI, EGD, RUQ ultrasound and 
gastric emptying studies that have only shown gastritis and 
H.pylori infection. She has had recent CT head to rule out 
neurological source at last admission which was within normal 
limits. She was about to be discharged from the hospital on 
___ when she was tolerating regular diet but was found in 
the lobby complaining again of back pain and nausea and was 
brought back to the floor.  Symptoms waned again as psychiatric 
evaluation began and initiated plan for discharge to inpatient 
psych.  Patient had been off IV anti-emetics or analgesics for 
>48 hrs at time of discharge.  She was tolerating full, bland 
diet.  She had tramadol available for occasional abdominal 
pains.     

# Depression/anxiety: Pt was seen by social work while in house. 
 She had been connected to a community ___ specialist and 
with an outpatient therapist through ___ but had 
missed numerous appointments.  She was repeatedly re-admitted to 
the hospital for N/V and back pain and was seen by psychiatric 
consult team several times for concern that her 
depression/anxiety were playing a large role in her symptoms.  
Patient also acknowledged to SW that depression/ anxiety were 
primary obstacles to her accessing outpatient primary care, GI 
care, or psychiatric care.  Therefore, given psychiatric 
comorbidities were driving negative cycle of inability to access 
___ medical care and seemed to play a significant role in 
symptom exacerbations psychiatry was consulted and thought 
patient met criteria for inpatient ps___ admission for symptom 
stabilization.  Therefore, she is being transferred to a crisis 
center to facilitate voluntary psychiatric admission.  Patient 
was continued on her home sertraline and lorazepam in house.     
 

# Chronic lower back pain s/p MVA: Pt has had multiple 
admissions for acute on chronic lower back pain s/p MVA.  She 
initially received IV dilaudid on admission, mixed with 50cc 
normal saline and infused slowly.  She was quickly weaned off 
the IV dilaudid and transitioned to po tylenol and tramadol 
which was started on low dose and uptitrated to 50mg TID prn.  
She was also given lidocaine patch on her back for pain.  She 
was evaluated by physical therapy and was able to ambulate 
without difficulty.  ___ recommended outpatient physical therapy 
for core strenghtening.  She was pain-free for the majority of 
the time but also had acute exacerbations of her pain, again 
associated with N/V and emotional distress.  On exam, she was 
largely nontender on palpation of lumbar spine and paraspinal 
muscles and had negative straight leg raise b/l.   She was 
discharged home on tramadol for pain.  

# DMI: Pt with history of type 1 DM.  She wsa followed by ___ 
consult team while in the hospital.   Blood sugars ranged widely 
from ___ when NPO in the morning to as high as 400s.  This was 
likely related to variable diet as pt was NPO at times and 
tolerating diet at other times.  She was initially given smaller 
doses of her home lantus when NPO, leading to elevated blood 
sugars the following day.  However, by time of discharge, per 
___ consult recs, she was put on home dose of lantus and 
HISS.  Blood glucose on this regimen fell to ___ she was 
symptomatic at this time, complaining of lightheadedness, and 
improved with juice.  She was discharged home on smaller dose of 
lantus 28 units qhs.  She was continued on her home dose of 
aspirin.

# Urine culture: U/A showed no nitrites/leukocytes or bacteria 
but urine culture grew >100,000 coagulase negative 
staphlycoccus.  Pt denied dysuria or frequency.  Given her 
diabetes, this was likely asymptomatic bacteruria and she was 
not treated with antibiotics for this.

# HTN: BP ranged widely from systolic 100s to 170s throughout 
hospital stay, often elevated when symptomatic from N/V, back 
pain, and anxiety.  Diastolic BPs were also elevated to 100s.  
She should follow up with her PCP to monitor her BP and start 
antihypertensives as outpatient as needed.

# H.pylori: Pt had recent EGD in ___ that showed gastritis 
and biopsies consistent with H.pylori.  She had been started on 
antibiotics for H.pylori but reportedly only completed a one 
week course.  Because she had been admitted with N/V, it was 
decided not to re-initiate antibiotic therapy during hospital 
admission as this would have exacerbated her symptoms.  She was 
discharged with follow-up at ___ clinic.

Discharge Instructions:
It was a pleasure taking care of you at the hospital. You were 
admitted with back pain and nausea/vomiting similar to your 
previous episodes of gastroparesis.  Your back pain was treated 
initially with IV hydromorphone and you were transitioned to 
oral pain medications.  You were seen by our physical therapist 
who felt that you would likely benefit from outpatient physical 
therapy.  You should talk with your primary care doctor about ___ 
referral for outpatient physical therapy.  

For your nausea/vomiting, you were given iv anti-nausea 
medications and pain medicines.  You were feeling better by time 
of discharge and able to eat without feeling nauseous.  Please 
continue a bland diet for a few days while recovering from your 
nausea/vomiting.  Please also follow-up at the ___ 
clinic.  You have a stomach infection called H pylori that 
causes irritation and for which you need further treatment.  
Because the medications for this can cause nausea we are 
postponing therapy for now.  You should discuss this at your 
gastroenterology follow-up.  
.

2) Tramadol 50mg three times a day as needed for pain was
